A1-A2.headline: The Big World Of American Football

pages.text:
The National Football League is the top American football group in the United States. It began in 1920 and took its new name in 1922.

Today, it has 32 teams in two halves, with its main office in New York.
pages.caption: Roger Goodell is the NFL commissioner.

evidence.articleCaption: Roger Goodell, National Football League Commissioner since 2006 (pictured in 2012)

pages.text:
Each year has warm-up games, an 18-week main season, and a final round for the top teams. Every team plays 17 regular games to earn a spot.

The long year ends with the Super Bowl, one huge game for the title. This plan makes sure only the best teams reach the very last match.

Every April, the NFL holds a big event to pick new college players. Each club keeps up to 55 players, with 48 ready on game days.

This system helps every team add young stars and keep games close all year.
pages.caption: A player is picked in the draft.

evidence.articleCaption: Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza, the first overall pick of the 2026 NFL draft

pages.text:
The NFL is the richest sports group in the world, and millions of fans love it. Its matches are among the most-watched TV shows in the United States.

By joining fast, exciting play with huge TV reach, the league stays one of the strongest forces in modern world sport today.

B1-B2.headline: Inside The Professional World Of American Football

pages.text:
The National Football League stands as the top professional football body in the United States. Founded in 1920, it adopted its current name in 1922.

Based in New York, it now runs 32 teams across two conferences.
pages.caption: Roger Goodell, NFL Commissioner since 2006.

evidence.articleCaption: Roger Goodell, National Football League Commissioner since 2006 (pictured in 2012)

pages.text:
The yearly schedule moves through a preseason, an 18-week regular season, and a knockout playoff round. Every team competes in 17 regular games.

The campaign finishes with the Super Bowl championship match. This clear structure guarantees that only the strongest squads contend for the title.

Each April, the NFL holds a player draft to pick top college athletes. Rosters hold up to 55 players, with 48 active on game days.

This process lets clubs refresh talent yearly and maintain fair balance league-wide.
pages.caption: Fernando Mendoza, the 2026 NFL draft pick.

evidence.articleCaption: Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza, the first overall pick of the 2026 NFL draft

pages.text:
As the wealthiest professional sports league on earth, the NFL draws massive public attention. Its weekly broadcasts rank among the most-watched television programs across the United States.

By pairing elite athletic contests with broad media coverage, the league remains a dominant force in global sport.

C1-C2.headline: The Evolution And Structure Of The National Football League

pages.text: The National Football League represents the preeminent professional American football institution. Established in 1920 and renamed in 1922, its New York headquarters governs 32 franchises across two conferences.
pages.caption: Roger Goodell, NFL Commissioner since 2006.

evidence.articleCaption: Roger Goodell, National Football League Commissioner since 2006 (pictured in 2012)

pages.text:
The annual calendar encompasses exhibition fixtures, an 18-week regular schedule of 17 contests per franchise, and an elimination tournament.

Culminating in the Super Bowl championship, this competitive architecture ensures that solely the highest-performing clubs vie for ultimate supremacy.

Every April, the league administers an amateur draft to allocate collegiate prospects. Squads cap rosters at 55 personnel, designating 48 active participants per fixture.

Such parity mechanisms sustain competitive equilibrium.
pages.caption: Fernando Mendoza, top 2026 NFL draft pick.

evidence.articleCaption: Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza, the first overall pick of the 2026 NFL draft

pages.text:
Commanding unmatched commercial revenue worldwide, the NFL wields extraordinary cultural prominence. Its televised spectacles consistently dominate American broadcast ratings.

Through synthesizing rigorous athletic execution with expansive media distribution, the organization preserves enduring supremacy across professional athletics.

glossary.en_def: a huge, powerful, and overwhelming force
